ASCII only: scripts/check.sh greps tests/fixtures/* for non-ASCII bytes.
PO-11 / D-PLY-7: where the player may write. mpv's own key bindings are
live on its window - `s` screenshots, `Q` writes a resume record - and
both used to land wherever the shell happened to be, in $HOME, at 0644.
cwd is the runtime directory so an unanticipated relative write is
private and gone at logout; screenshots are DURABLE because the user
asked for that file; watch-later is a resume position for a live stream
and is never worth keeping. D-PLY-10 / CL2 adds shader-cache: mpv's own
shader and ICC caches default into $XDG_CACHE_HOME/mpv/, outside this
plugin's tree; both are content-free and regenerable, so they are
contained in the runtime directory and are ephemeral on purpose.
Run by Model.playerDirs and player_dirs().

_comment: state.json `session` (section 8, ruling PO-3): the record the service
writes on play and clears on stop, read back by Model.parseState and by
normalize_state. `state` is the whole document as it sits on disk,
`record` is what both readers must produce for its `session` key.
The four keys of a state file are deliberately exercised together: the
CLI rewrites the whole document, so a reader that drops the key would
erase a running player's record on the next `state favorite add`.
session.name: a full record round-trips through both readers
a file written before the key exists reads as no session
a version-1 file (0.1.0) has no session either
an explicit null is the cleared state the service writes on stop
a record without an id is not a channel and is dropped
a record that is not an object is dropped
an id on its own is enough: name and clock default
a numeric name and a string clock are coerced, not dropped
a fractional clock truncates toward zero in both languages
an unparsable clock is zero, never an error
the session rides beside the other keys and none of them lose it

_comment: `player probe` stdout: what the helper WRITES and what Model.parsePlayerProbe
READS, as one document instead of two hand-written copies.
M2-05 made this load-bearing. The service takes the window-owning mpv pid
from `probe.pid` and refuses picture in picture without it (addressing by
class alone would float, shrink and pin a stranger's mpv, PLY-RST-11), and
it reads it DEFENSIVELY - notePlayerPid ignores anything that is not a
positive integer. So a helper that stopped emitting `pid`, or renamed it,
would not raise anything anywhere: the pid would stay 0 and the p key would
answer `Nothing playing` while a channel was plainly playing. Both sides run
this vector, so the key name is a contract rather than a coincidence:
tests/test_player.py asserts a REAL probe emits exactly these keys with a
pid that is the player's own, and tests/Model.test.js asserts the parser
reads them back.
`claimed` is emitted but not parsed - the shell does not act on it - which
is why `parsed` names every field the model does produce rather than
mirroring the reply key for key.

stopLadder.name: idle -> quit over IPC, then the quit grace
quit ignored -> SIGTERM, then the kill grace
SIGTERM ignored -> SIGKILL, nothing left to arm
after SIGKILL only the exit is awaited

endedVerdict.name: the user stopped it: silent, whatever mpv reported
a stop ladder is running: silent
the user pressed q in mpv: silent, as exit 0 is today
clean end of stream: silent stop (PO-4, zero behaviour change)
dead stream: notify with the file_error
error with no file_error falls back to the generic reason
reason stop with no user stop: a load we issued was replaced, then it died
redirect is never terminal (the .m3u8 masters IPTV uses most)
no end-file at all (crash, SIGKILL): notify with the generic reason
fail open: a missing entry id never suppresses the failure
fail open: an unknown entry id never suppresses the failure
an unknown reason is treated as a failure, never swallowed
a file_error carrying a URL is redacted to its host
endedVerdict._comment: The two redactors differ in shape on purpose and have since v0.1: redact_urls() in python keeps scheme://host (it is also the helper's stdout/stderr filter), Model.redactUrls reduces to the host alone. Both drop the userinfo, the port, the path and the query, and QML redacts a second time, so the two converge at the sink. verdictPython pins the python shape rather than pretending they are identical.
